Twin of the Kotlin UserProfile.cacheKey in android/app/src/main/java/com/noop/analytics/AnalyticsModels.kt; the two types sit in differently named files, so the ledger cannot pair them.

Twin of the Kotlin `val OuraSpO2.channel` in android/app/src/main/java/com/noop/oura/OuraEvents.kt. Both are one-line extension properties over OuraSpO2 returning OuraSpO2Channel, added together in the same change. Kotlin declares its copy as a TOP-LEVEL extension property with a dotted receiver, which the ledger's Kotlin property scan does not index, so the Swift side reads as one-sided. The pair is real; only one half is visible to the inventory.

Room @Query DAO method. The Swift store issues the equivalent SQL inline in WhoopStore Reads.swift / StreamStore.swift rather than through a DAO, so there is no Swift function to pair with; its WHOOP 5 siblings whoop5RrIntervals, hasWhoop5RrSource and promoteWhoop5RrSource are one-sided for the same architectural reason.

Room Migration.migrate override of MIGRATION_40_41 (#2371). GRDB registers each migration as a closure (`v47-rr-whoop5-fill`), so there is no Swift function to pair with; the two are paired by the migration identifiers pinned in schema_oracle.json and by the SQL constant pair WHOOP5_RR_FILL_MIGRATION_SQL / WhoopStore.whoop5RrFillMigrationSQL.

Consumed only by the Apple OuraLiveSource screen-off live-HR suspend (Experimental "All-day heart rate & HRV"), to stand the daytime-HR hold down for the learned night instead of for every screen-off. Android's OuraLiveSource.kt has no screen-off suspend (#1546), so there is nothing for a Kotlin twin to gate; per review, Android stays without it until that suspend exists, at which point this becomes a twin.

The added preserveUnscoredHistory argument matches the role of analyzeRecent in the excluded Swift app layer. This records the new Kotlin orchestration signature, not a byte-identity claim.
The additional HR input feeds offWristIntervals during Android stream preparation; Swift performs the corresponding read and wear reconciliation inline in the excluded app-layer analyzeRecent.

The shared repair delegates to the scorer with cached-only preservation. Swift runEffortRescoreIfNeeded/runHistoryRepairIfNeeded perform that role in the excluded app layer; signatures differ by platform dependencies.

Swift groups daily metrics, metric points and provenance by day inline in app-layer analyzeRecent. Kotlin extracts that persistence preparation as a test seam; this is a role twin, not a function parity claim.
Swift IntelligenceEngine.historyRepairIsPending has the same repair-flag gate in the excluded app layer; both have direct truth-table coverage.
Swift app-layer analyzeRecent performs the conditional per-day persistence loop inline. Kotlin extracts it to keep the instrumented scoring coroutine below the bytecode budget.

This Kotlin extension dispatches a computed window to repository persistence. The corresponding persistComputedScores dispatch is inline in the excluded Swift app-layer analyzeRecent; this records its architectural role.

Swift Repository.refresh reads the same imported daily union (unionDailyMetrics) in the excluded app layer and hands it, still apart from the computed union, to ChargeBaselines.resolve (#2525); this disposition does not assert behavioral parity.

Kotlin nests the drained sum under BroopEnergyEngine.Summary, while Swift owns it on EnergyDaySummary. Both sum the same three drains and are oracle-tested; differently named type owners prevent lexical property pairing.

Android maps its Room-backed StressMonitor epochs into BroopEnergyEngine.DayInput; Swift EnergyReservoir.day accepts the native Swift stress type directly. This is a type adapter, with the integrated values pinned by the body oracle.

Kotlin exposes summary serialization as a method while Swift EnergyDaySummary.storedPairs is a computed property. The exact keys and rounded values are exercised by the Swift-generated body oracle; the inventory does not pair across declaration kinds.

Kotlin names its input BroopMindDay to coexist with the Android model, while Swift names it MindDay. The same measured-minute and finite-input gate is included in the body oracle; only the declaring type name differs.

One Kotlin Boolean dispatch entry combines the separate Swift ResilienceEngine.history and CumulativeStressEngine.history functions. Both numeric paths have Swift-generated oracle cases; the extra dispatch is a Kotlin API representation.

The exact shared stress/Rest history completion key is declared on the excluded Swift IntelligenceEngine extension. Kotlin keeps it beside its cancellable history-repair coordinator; completion semantics have focused tests.

The matching Swift RestScoringPrefs.consistencyKey preference/metric key is declared in the excluded app layer. Kotlin stores the identical key with the pure Rest implementation; this records its different source-layer location.

The matching Swift RestScoringPrefs.v2Key preference/metric key is declared in the excluded app layer. Kotlin stores the identical key with the pure Rest implementation; this records its different source-layer location.

The matching Swift RestScoringPrefs.hoursVsNeedKey preference/metric key is declared in the excluded app layer. Kotlin stores the identical key with the pure Rest implementation; this records its different source-layer location.

java.time requires an explicit normalization adapter to match Foundation DateComponents overflow behavior. Swift performs this inline in SleepRegularity.windowStart and dayKey; the Kotlin parser is a separate implementation detail covered by the regularity oracle.

Android org.json stage records are converted into half-open wake ranges before the pure regularity timeline runs. Swift receives typed sleep-stage intervals from its app model, so this JSON adapter has no pure-package function counterpart.

Kotlin explicitly parses a persisted raw goal into enum entries. Swift synthesizes Goal.init(rawValue:) for its raw-value enum; this parser supplies the same default without introducing a separate target formula.

Kotlin has an explicit sign-aware rounding adapter for Swift Double.rounded() tie behavior. It is used by the stored stress summary and verified against the literal Swift stress oracle, rather than representing a different stress calculation.

Kotlin NightAggregate serialization is a function while the Swift NightAggregate.storedPairs endpoint is a computed property. The stress oracle pins the shared keys and values; the inventory cannot pair a function with a property.

Kotlin DayResult serialization is a function while the Swift DayResult.storedPairs endpoint is a computed property. The stress oracle pins the shared keys and values; the inventory cannot pair a function with a property.

Kotlin StressDaySummary serialization is a function while the Swift StressDaySummary.storedPairs endpoint is a computed property. The stress oracle pins the shared keys and values; the inventory cannot pair a function with a property.
The Swift analysis post-loop appends Rest and optional component rows inline. Kotlin extracts those same serial appends to remain below the instrumented JVM method budget.
Swift gathers stored and just-scored sleep sessions before its stressRestPass call. Kotlin isolates that preparation and Room reads from the pure reductions to preserve the JVM method budget.
Swift passes the resolved consistency and sleep-stress values into RestV2 in the app-layer scoring pass. Kotlin owns that lookup on the immutable pass result before invoking the paired composite.

Swift retains cached aggregate values when raw HR is absent and replaces them for present raw inputs in its stressRestPass. Kotlin extracts that branch as a pure test seam; no missing-data gate is waived.
Swift groups stored and newly staged sleep blocks by their local wake day in its app-layer stress setup. Kotlin makes that local-date conversion a named helper.
The Swift app-layer analysis prepares the inclusive calendar-day window before stressRestPass. Kotlin names that calendar enumeration separately to test daylight-saving boundaries.

Android retains the legacy Result.contributions compatibility view for existing Kotlin readers. Canonical v2 results use the shared ageDelta and impacts fields; this alias adds no model calculation or stored key.

Android retains the legacy Result.deltaYears compatibility view for existing Kotlin readers. Canonical v2 results use the shared ageDelta and impacts fields; this alias adds no model calculation or stored key.

Android retains Healthspan.bodyAge as a compatibility projection for existing Kotlin consumers. The canonical v2 current/projected result and oracle remain shared with Swift; the alias is not an independent stored value.

Swift vitalityVO2Points defines the positive-value/date filter as a local closure; Kotlin uses a local function inside the paired helper. The source choice and boundaries are covered by the Healthspan oracle.

Android retains Healthspan.recentBodyAge as a compatibility projection for existing Kotlin consumers. The canonical v2 current/projected result and oracle remain shared with Swift; the alias is not an independent stored value.

This Kotlin data-layer file combines the excluded Swift weekly update and first-history backfill dispatch. The shared Healthspan model and repository reader are independently paired and oracle-tested.

Swift separates writeWeeklyHealthspan from runHealthspanV2BackfillIfNeeded; Kotlin dispatches the first Sunday-history fill and later weekly updates through one Room helper. Serial canonical reads and writes have a separate regression guard.

Android gathers Health Connect and imported Apple Health body series through a local source adapter. Swift gathers Apple Health directly in its repository. Lab precedence and lean-mass conversion stay in the paired, oracle-tested helper.

The Swift HealthspanSnapshot.delta computed property is in the excluded app layer. Kotlin keeps the same single-snapshot age subtraction in its data layer; this disposition records the scope boundary.

The Swift backfillPoints loop and weekly writer live in the excluded app layer. Kotlin gathers history once and emits the same gated Sunday triples from its repository layer; the age clock and model are shared.

Swift Repository.allSleepSessions merges imported/computed blocks by local wake-day coverage. The main Kotlin repository already pairs to that function; this stress-store adapter accepts explicit epoch bounds and preserves the same source precedence.

Android exposes a result-only wrapper around its witness-bearing stress analysis so UI readers do not depend on Room cache metadata. The actual computation is paired to Swift Repository.stressDayAnalysis; this wrapper only unwraps the result.

This Android-only local memo-signature encoder writes an optional IEEE-754 value into the digest. The signature is in-memory cache state, not a physiological value, cross-platform dedup key, or backup field.

Android keeps an ephemeral SHA-256 memo witness over fetched Room sensor rows, masks and prior aggregates. It is never persisted or exported across platforms; Swift uses its own repository cache revision. Numeric stress output remains governed separately.

This Android-only local memo-signature encoder writes the ordered interval mask into the digest. The signature is in-memory cache state, not a physiological value, cross-platform dedup key, or backup field.
The Android reader limits its weak, in-memory Room analysis memo to 96 days. This cache-size cap is platform-local and does not change any stress window or stored result.

This Android-only local memo-signature encoder writes one little-endian integer into the digest. The signature is in-memory cache state, not a physiological value, cross-platform dedup key, or backup field.
The Android Room stress reader caps fetched sensor arrays at 250000 rows per local-day request. This is an Android query resource bound, not a shared stress formula or persisted field.

Android resolves Room raw-source keys from its active device registry and canonical import id before reading stress inputs. Swift has different store ownership plumbing; this helper adds no stress math and uses the existing Android registry resolver.

This Android-only local memo-signature encoder writes a length-delimited UTF-8 string into the digest. The signature is in-memory cache state, not a physiological value, cross-platform dedup key, or backup field.

The Swift repository computes local wake-day coverage inline while merging sleep blocks. Kotlin gives this conversion a local name in the stress reader; its timezone is the same one used for the requested day bounds.

Android Room exposes one transactional replacement API for daily/provenance rows and explicitly declared metric-only stress/energy rows. Swift WhoopStore uses GRDB persistComputedScores plus its specialized series path; the storage API shapes differ, not the score formulas.

The excluded Swift Healthspan reader fetches finished Lift Log sessions from its store. Kotlin isolates the active/archived/canonical Room union in the repository; the underlying single-source DAO read is paired to WhoopStore.liftSessions.

Android forwards a full computed-window request into the Room transaction API, including the metric-only key boundary. Swift uses its GRDB store directly from the app layer; this is the repository/storage forwarding seam.

Android must wrap the per-day history repair replacements in one cancellable Room transaction. Swift writes through GRDB transaction closures inside WhoopStore, so no repository transaction-forwarding function is required there.

Swift healthspanHistory gathers day inputs and lean mass in one app-layer reader. Kotlin separates this day-source read from its HealthspanRepository lean-mass read; scalar shaping, source choice and lift dedup have their own exact twins and oracle coverage.

The excluded Swift rescoreForRestModeChange uses the same 4000-day history default. Kotlin names that orchestration bound beside its cancellable repair helper; it is not the unrelated StandReminder history window.

Android wraps the displayed sleep fragments and their individual tombstone operations in one cancellable Room transaction. Swift BroopSleepInteractions performs the same per-fragment delete or undo through its app-layer loop; the extra repository batch boundary prevents partial Android writes and has rollback tests.

Android wraps the displayed sleep fragments and their individual tombstone operations in one cancellable Room transaction. Swift BroopSleepInteractions performs the same per-fragment delete or undo through its app-layer loop; the extra repository batch boundary prevents partial Android writes and has rollback tests.

Swift app-layer pass 2 appends the same SpO2 candidate, HRV overcount and primary-session RHR witness rows inline. Kotlin extracts those serial appends into a separate helper to stay below the instrumented scoring-coroutine method budget; it adds no computed signal or metric key.

Swift app-layer pass 2 appends the same SpO2 candidate, HRV overcount and primary-session RHR witness rows inline. Kotlin extracts those serial appends into a separate helper to stay below the instrumented scoring-coroutine method budget; it adds no computed signal or metric key.

Swift app-layer scoring pass maps detector sleep sessions to cached rows inline. Kotlin extracts the same source id, interval, efficiency, RHR, HRV, encoded stages and sparse-coverage fields to stay below the instrumented coroutine method budget; the helper introduces no staging formula or stored field.

Swift IntelligenceEngine builds its published Computed day from the persisted daily fields inside its app-layer pass. Kotlin isolates that exact day, recovery, strain, sleep duration, HRV and resting-HR projection to preserve the JVM instrumented method budget; this adapter does not recalculate or store any value.
